function: p. 1: Joint learned design of the base station precoder and the RIS phase shifts, with coupled amplitude and phase, to maximize the sum rate in a multi-RIS multiuser downlink.
system: p. 4: BS with 16 antennas, four passive reflecting RISs of 16 elements with practical amplitude-phase coupling, 1-4 single-antenna UEs per RIS, mmWave (carrier frequency not stated).
method: p. 3: DDPG actor-critic reinforcement learning with fully connected networks; state is UE presence, previous action and rates; trained with random or fixed numbers of users.
data_channel: p. 2, 4: Simulated mmWave Saleh-Valenzuela channels; path-loss parameters from 3GPP Release 16 [19], angles from [20]; RIS-BS 100 m, RIS-UE 2 m; no external dataset.
test_conditions: p. 4-5: Trained with random (1-4 per RIS) or fixed (2 or 4 per RIS) UEs; tested on random 4-16 UEs and other Pmax over 1,000 channel realizations.
baselines: p. 4: Non-learned: BCD [17], WMMSE-PI [18]. Learned: DDQN [4]. The paper says all three apply to a single RIS with fixed UEs and ideal reflection.
metrics: p. 4-5: Achievable sum rate (bps/Hz) versus Pmax, training reward versus episodes, percentage rate gains between schemes, FLOPs.
complexity: p. 4-5: Proposed DDPG requires 3.71e6 FLOPs on average at inference; BCD requires 7.03e8 FLOPs.
openness: p. 1-5: none; no link to code or data is given.
q1_support: p. 2: "followed the mmWave Saleh-Valenzuela (SV) channel model"; p. 4: "path loss parameters for the mmWave channel" come from 3GPP Release 16 [19], so only the path loss is taken from 3GPP.
q2_support: p. 5: "The trained weights used from these three scenarios were applicable to the scenario of the random UE number"; models trained with 2 or 4 fixed UEs are tested with random 4-16 UEs.
q3_support: p. 4: "compares the achievable rates of the proposed DDPG with those of two optimization-based algorithms" (BCD, WMMSE-PI) and DDQN [4]; p. 5: "DDPG outperformed DDQN by 63%".
q4_support: p. 4: "the proposed DDPG requires 3.71 × 10^6 floating-point operations (FLOPs) on average" (p. 5 adds 7.03 × 10^8 FLOPs for BCD).
q5_support: p. 4: "The following setup was considered in the simulations"; the data come from the paper's own simulator and no page gives a code or data link.
notes: The PDF is the arXiv preprint 2509.25661v1 (30 Sep 2025) with a template header (Vol. 14, No. 1, Jan. 2024); it prints no DOI, so the match with the DOI rests on the title and the letter format. The text layer of pages 4-5 is incomplete, so the quotes of q2, q3 and q4 (p. 4-5) were read from page images. q1: 3GPP TR 38.901 [19] gives only the path-loss parameters of a custom Saleh-Valenzuela simulator, so q1 is 0; reviewer may confirm. The text (p. 4) says BCD, WMMSE-PI and DDQN apply only to a single RIS with ideal reflection, yet Fig. 4 (p. 5) also plots DDQN multi-RIS curves; the comparison is on the achievable rate.
